claims.statement_verbatim: Every power of two reaches 1 under the standard Collatz function: for f(n) = n/2 if n even, 3n+1 if n odd, and for every k >= 0, iterating f starting from 2^k eventually reaches 1.
claims.conclusion: there exists m such that f applied m times to 2^k equals 1
surrounding_definitions: f: N -> N (called collatzStep in the Lean formalization), f(n) = n/2 if n even, 3n+1 if n odd -- this is the STANDARD (uncompressed) Collatz map, distinct from Eliahou's compressed map T used in VCE-001

proof_structure.inductive_step: 2^(k+1) is even, one step of f sends it to 2^k; by induction hypothesis 2^k reaches 1 in m more steps, so 2^(k+1) reaches 1 in m+1 steps

notes: This is a deliberately elementary, self-contained claim (no external paper, no supporting lemma chain) -- a genuine contrast case to VCE-001's multi-lemma, paper-derived claim. It exercises the FCVE pipeline's 'simple case' path.
